n: The psalmist asks God to remember David and all the hardships he endured — especially his devotion to finding a home for the ark of the covenant.

f.g: Hardships, or the trouble he took.

n: David made a solemn vow to ‘the Mighty One of Jacob,’ an ancient title of God.
He vowed not to rest in the comfort of his own house…

f.w: I will not give sleep to mine eyes

n: …until he found a dwelling place for the Lord. David longed to build a temple, though God let his son Solomon build it.

f.w: an habitation for the mighty God of Jacob

n: The worshipers recall the ark’s story: they heard of it in Ephrathah (the Bethlehem region) and found it in ‘the fields of Jaar,’ likely Kiriath-jearim, where it rested for years.
‘Let us go to his dwelling and worship at his footstool’ — the ark, pictured as the footrest of God’s throne.
These words echo the call Moses used when the ark set out: ‘Arise, O LORD!’ Solomon used them at the temple dedication.

f.w: Arise, O LORD, into thy rest

f.g: The ark, symbol of God’s mighty presence.

n: May the priests be dressed in righteousness and the faithful shout for joy.
For David’s sake, don’t reject the current king, the Lord’s anointed.

f.w: turn not away the face of thine anointed

n: God made a sure oath to David: one of his own descendants would sit on his throne. Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus Christ.

f.w: Of the fruit of thy body

n: The promise had a condition: if David’s children kept God’s covenant, their line would rule forever.

f.w: If thy children will keep my covenant

n: The Lord chose Zion and desired it as his home.
God speaks: ‘This is my resting place forever; here I will live.’

f.w: This is my rest for ever

n: God promises abundant food for Zion, so even her poor will have bread.

f.w: I will satisfy her poor with bread

n: God answers verse 9 with something greater: her priests will be clothed not only with righteousness but with salvation.
God will make a ‘horn’ — a strong king — sprout from David’s line, and keep a lamp burning for him. The ‘branch’ and ‘lamp’ became messianic images.

f.w: the horn of David to bud

n: David’s enemies will be clothed with shame, but his crown will shine. Contrasting ‘clothing’ runs through the psalm.

f.g: His crown will sparkle or bloom.
